text: In metabolic flux modeling, what does the null space of the stoichiometric matrix S represent?
choices: The set of thermodynamically favorable reactions only
The list of essential genes in the network
The feasible steady-state flux distributions (the flux cone) satisfying mass balance
The eigenvector centrality of each metabolite
explanation: At steady state S*v = 0, so the null space of S contains exactly the flux vectors v that satisfy mass balance -- this is the feasible flux cone exploited by flux balance analysis (FBA). Thermodynamic favorability is a separate constraint layered on top of the stoichiometric null space, essential genes are identified by simulating reaction knockouts rather than read directly off the null space, and eigenvector centrality is a graph-theory concept for network nodes, unrelated to stoichiometry.
